Germany receives first F-35 warplane at ceremony in US. Germany has taken delivery of the first of its F-35 stealth warplanes at a ceremony in Texas. The event marks a significant development in Germany’s defense strategy.

New France boss Zidane confirms Mbappe as captain after naming first squad. Zinedine Zidane has appointed Kylian Mbappe as captain of the French national team. This decision follows Zidane’s recent appointment as the new head coach succeeding Didier Deschamps.

US to ‘soon’ deport Ecuador assassination suspect: minister. Ecuadoran businessman Xavier Jordan, suspected of orchestrating the assassination of presidential candidate Fernando Villavicencio, is set to be deported from the US soon.

US deportees to Equatorial Guinea were arrested and beaten by police, lawyers say. Ahmed Soliman from Egypt and Samson Birhane from Eritrea were arrested and mistreated in Equatorial Guinea after being deported from the US. Over 40 people have been deported under similar agreements, raising concerns among rights groups.

Syria arrests 5 Assad-era air force officers over strikes on populated areas. DAMASCUS: Syrian security forces have arrested five former air force officers accused of involvement in deadly airstrikes on populated areas during the country’s civil war under ousted President Bashar Assad. DEIR AL-BALAH: The deadly collapse of a multi-story building in Gaza has drawn new attention to the hardships facing Palestinians there nearly a year after a ceasefire between Israel and Hamas promised to kick-start reconstruction. But as talks faltered, rebuilding plans stalled. Israel bars entry of almost all construction materials, making even repairs difficult. The US State Department said Thursday it was refusing to grant visas to Abbas and other Palestinian officials for next week’s assembly. Russian attack kills two in Balakliia in eastern Ukraine. A Russian attack in Balakliia, northeastern Ukraine, resulted in the deaths of two individuals and injuries to two others. The attack also caused a fire and damaged homes.

US gives UN more time to end support for Somalia peacekeepers. MOGADISHU: The US has agreed to give the UN another year to wind down its support for African peacekeepers in Somalia, a document showed — a move that gives some breathing space to a force that feared quicker cuts, but still leaves its future in peril. The annual Medusa exercise, led by Greece and Egypt, ended on a strip of coastline outside the port city of Chania. RIYADH: Saudi Arabia’s Interior Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Saud bin Naif met on Thursday in Riyadh with Minister of Interior and Commander of the Internal Security Force (Lekhwiya) of Qatar Sheikh Khalifa bin Hamad bin Khalifa Al-Thani. RIYADH: The Saudi aid agency KSrelief has signed an agreement with the Refaq Association in Hail to meet basic needs and provide care for orphans in Djibouti. Cuba hit with seventh major blackout of the year. Cuba experienced its seventh significant blackout this year due to fuel shortages and outdated thermoelectric plants. The energy ministry reported a total system disconnection but did not specify the cause.

Death toll passes 100 soldiers in Mali attack last week: sources. Over 100 soldiers were reportedly killed in a jihadist attack on the Malian army’s Dioura camp, marking one of the deadliest assaults in the ongoing conflict.

Bayern star Kane becomes fastest player to score 100 Bundesliga goals. Harry Kane set a new Bundesliga record by scoring 100 goals in just 98 matches, surpassing the previous record held by Cologne’s Dieter Muller.

Veolia signs 3 agreements on water, waste and decarbonization in Saudi Arabia. "We can paint murals bigger than this to express our feelings." Macklemore, who has long supported Palestinian causes, was cut from British pop star Sheeran's musical lineup over remarks on stage criticizing Israel's military assault in Gaza. Macron said that the aim of the meeting was to strengthen cooperation and avoid unnecessary tensions between G7 countries and their key partners. 'Our commitment is unconditional': Amid Houthi attacks, DG ISPR says Pakistan will 'go to any extent' to defend Saudi Arabia. Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry has said that Pakistan will go to “any extent” to defend Saudi Arabia, adding that Islamabad’s commitment to the kingdom’s security is “unconditional”. He made the remarks in an interview with Arab News , clips of which were posted on its social media account on X on Friday. The remarks come as fighting between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthis has intensified, with the group making gains along Yemen’s Red Sea coast near the strategic waterway and launching missile and drone attacks on Saudi territory, while Riyadh has stepped up airstrikes against Houthi positions. This week, the Saudi-led coalition battling the Houthis accused the rebels of targeting the holy city of Makkah, sparking outrage across the Muslim world. However, the Houthis swiftly rejected Riyadh’s report as a “lie”. “Pakistan fully stands with the kingdom of Saudi Arabia, both diplomatically and physically. And I would like to underscore the word physically,” Lt Gen Chaudhry said in the interview with Arab News . “We will go to any extent for the security of Haramain Sharifain and the kingdom of Saudi Arabia. To any extent as asked and required by our Saudi brothers,” he said. “It should be clear that the people of Pakistan stand shoulder to shoulder with their Saudi brothers and sisters. There should be no doubt about it,” he said. “So, in a nutshell, we are there and will continue to defend the kingdom of Saudi Arabia against any aggression,” he said. The military’s spokesperson added that Pakistan’s politico-military leadership remained in continuous contact and engagement with the Saudi leadership. He said that at the same time, Pakistan, “very earnestly and sincerely”, was working with the help of regional countries and others to find a “negotiated, peaceful outcome of this complex situation”. “That’s where the position of Pakistan is,” he said. In another clip posted on X, he said Pakistan “remained not only committed, but we are already there for the protection of Haramain Sharifain and the kingdom of Saudi Arabia”. “We are there to protect them,” he asserted, reiterating that Pakistan would “go to any extent” as required by the Saudi leadership. “Our commitment to Saudi security is unconditional. It stems from a deep-rooted, historical and unbreakable bond between the people of Pakistan and the people of Saudi Arabia, between the political and the military leadership of both countries,” he said. “So, nothing stops us. Nothing bars us. Nothing is there which hesitates [sic] our commitment. So, whatever is required, whatever is asked, we will go to any extent for that,” he said. According to the write-up of the interview, Lt Gen Chaudhry was also asked about the phone call between Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Wednesday. “The politico-military leadership of Pakistan remains in continuous communication with the esteemed leadership of the kingdom of Saudi Arabia on all these matters,” he was quoted as saying by the publication. Lt Gen Chaudhry added that Islamabad was consulting regional governments to seek “a negotiated and peaceful outcome” to the wider crisis. He described the Islamabad memorandum of understanding between the United States and Iran in June as “a consensus document which we think provides the only real pathway forward for getting out of this complex military situation in which we are’. According to the publication, asked whether Pakistan expected to bring Washington and Tehran back to negotiations soon, the military spokesperson gave no timetable. He said Islamabad continued to search for common ground despite mistrust, “spoilers” and “detractors”. Pakistan and Saudi Arabia had signed the “ Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement ” in Riyadh last September, pledging that any attack on either nation would be treated as an act of aggression against both. Last month, the countries and Turkiye also signed the Makkah Defence Alliance, which stipulates that an attack on one member state would be treated as an attack on all. Its inaugural meeting was held in Istanbul on Aug 31, where it was decided that Pakistan would initially head the alliance’s secretariat for three years. Earlier this week, Lt Gen Chaudhry said that the Makkah defence pact had no “regional aspirations” and that it was intended for collective deterrence. “It is defensive. There’s nothing aggressive. There are no regional aspirations. It is collective deterrence,” he said in an interview with Al Arabiya English. Meanwhile, Foreign Office spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan on Thursday reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitments to Saudi Arabia’s security, but stressed that the Houthi conflict should be addressed through dialogue and diplomacy rather than through coercive means. “The Houthis must also stop their activities, and in this regard, our discussions basically revolve around bringing peace and stability through dialogue and diplomacy, and not through coercive measures,” he said. The FO spokesperson also said that Pakistan was committed “in intent and spirit” to implementing the agreements signed with Saudi Arabia. He nevertheless declined to disclose how Pakistan might respond operationally, saying such decisions involved matters of confidentiality.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday issued directives to include motorcycles, rickshaws and Qingqis that were registered after Jan 1, 2006 in the govt’s recently announced fuel scheme. “All motorcycles, rickshaws, and Qingqis registered after Jan 1, 2006, will be eligible for registration in the Prime Minister Fuel Relief Scheme,” the Prime Minister’s Office said in a post on the social media platform X. “Now, those who drive 20-year-old motorcycles, rickshaws, and Qingqis will also be able to benefit from the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme,” it said. PM Shehbaz Sharif had on Sep 13 announced a “relief scheme” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices. Under the scheme, owners of motorcycles, rickshaws, Qingqis, three-wheelers and vehicles with engines of up to 800cc will receive a Rs100 per litre relief on petrol. Motorcycles, rickshaws and Qingqis, as well as other two- and three-wheeler users, are eligible for relief on 20 litres of petrol per month. Owners of small cars with engines up to 800cc will receive the Rs100 per litre relief on 30 litres of petrol every month. Renewed hostilities in the Middle East, which have resulted in disruption of major oil supply routes, have caused fuel prices to rise in the past two months. In addition to the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz due to the US-Iran war, trade via Bab al-Mandab — which has become a vital route for Saudi oil exports in recent months — is also facing a rising threat from Houthi rebels. The subsidy scheme faced snags on Thursday, the first day of its nationwide rollout, as many petrol pumps declined to honour the digital app, claiming they lacked the system needed to provide petrol at Rs100 per litre less. A day prior, the Pakistan Petroleum Dealers Association (PPDA) expressed concerns that its members were unaware of the subsidy disbursement mechanism and feared they would have to run from pillar to post to recover the amount. Amid the fuel crisis, the federal government on Thursday also reintroduced austerity measures, including setting 9pm as the closing time for markets and reducing fuel provision for official vehicles by 50 per cent for a period of three months.

Lahore ATC disposes of petition by PTI leader Hammad Azhar’s mother, wife seeking permission to meet him. LAHORE: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Friday disposed of a petition filed on behalf of PTI leader Hammad Azhar’s mother and wife, seeking permission for them to meet the former federal minister, who is in police custody on physical remand in a May 9 case. ATC-IV Judge Sardar Muhammad Akram Khan passed the order on September 17. The petition sought directions to the relevant authorities to allow the petitioners to meet Azhar, who is confined in police lock-up, and to grant him access to legal counsel. In his order, the judge noted that, when asked, the prosecution’s counsel had no response regarding Rule 26.28 of the Police Rules, 1934 — the provision governing family and legal access to people in police custody. The judge also observed that the petitioners had earlier filed a similar writ petition before the Lahore High Court (LHC), which was dismissed as withdrawn, with liberty to seek a remedy before the appropriate forum. The judge further noted that the case file did not show that the petitioners had first approached the police under Rule 26.28 before moving the court. In light of this, the ATC judge directed the petitioners to submit a written application to the station house officer (SHO) of Sarwar Road police and instructed that, if approached, the SHO must strictly comply with the requirements of Rule 26.28 of the Police Rules, 1934. With these observations, the judge disposed of the petition. Advocate Zain Sheikh appeared for the petitioners and Deputy District Public Prosecutor Nayyar Naveed represented the state. Hammad Azhar was arrested in Multan earlier this month and handed over to Lahore police in connection with cases related to the May 9 riots, including the attack on Jinnah House. Azhar’s mother and wife had approached the ATC against the police for allegedly denying his family and lawyer access to him. Ishrat Azhar, the mother, and Marriam Hammad, the wife, had filed a joint petition through their counsel, Abuzar Salman Niazi.

'Petrol so expensive' that PTI lawmakers arrive at Sindh Assembly on donkey carts in protest. KARACHI: PTI lawmakers in Sindh arrived at the provincial assembly on donkey carts — in protest. “The ministers and [treasury] MPAs should also reach the assembly the same way on donkey carts,” PTI’s Sajjad Ali was seen saying in a video that showed him riding a donkey cart and holding a placard as he protested the “petrol bomb dropped on the people”. Other MPAs, led by Ali, also held placards and raised slogans against the federal government over the recent increase in petrol prices . They rode donkey carts from areas near the assembly to its main gate and demanded the government withdraw the increase in petroleum prices immediately. Speaking on the occasion, Ali said that the protest was aimed at highlighting the plight of the common man due to skyrocketing fuel prices. “Petrol has become so expensive that we cannot even come to the assembly in our vehicles,” he said, adding that the people were bearing the brunt of the government’s policies. Renewed hostilities in the Middle East, which have resulted in disruption of major oil supply routes, have caused fuel prices to rise in the past two months. Currently, the government adjusts fuel prices daily. After the latest change on Thursday, the price of petrol stands at Rs390.79 per litre while high-speed diesel (HSD) costs Rs424.92 per litre. These prices also include Rs114 per litre levied by the government in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. On Thursday, a joint meeting of the Executive Committee and Rules Committee of the Pakistan Bar Council (PBC) also strongly condemned the unprecedented daily increases in fuel prices, demanding that the government take measures to control the increases and provide relief to citizens. Under the scheme, motorcycles, rickshaws and Qingqis, as well as other two- and three-wheeler users, are eligible for relief on 20 litres of petrol per month. The owners of small cars with engines up to 800cc will receive the Rs100 per litre relief on 30 litres of petrol every month. The subsidy scheme faced snags on Thursday, the first day of its nationwide rollout, as many petrol pumps declined to honour the digital app launched for the purpose, claiming that they lacked the system needed to provide petrol at Rs100 per litre less. The same day, the federal government also reintroduced austerity measures, including setting 9pm as the closing time for markets and reducing fuel provision for official vehicles by 50 per cent for a period of three months.

IHC rules infringement of fundamental rights breaches Constitution ahead of PTI’s Sept 27 protest. ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) has ruled that any activity resulting in infringement of citizens’ fundamental rights amounts to a violation of the Constitution, warning that public office holders responsible for such violations would also be deemed to have breached their oath of office. The ruling came in a detailed 37-page judgment on a petition concerning the proposed nationwide PTI protest towards Islamabad on September 27, 2026. PTI had announced the march to demand release of party founder Imran Khan and mobilise people for the supremacy of the Constitution. A citizen, Waqas Ahmed, had challenged the planned move on the grounds that the protest could disrupt routine life, traffic and business activities in the federal capital. A three-member bench headed by Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar and comprising Justice Muhammad Asif and Justice Muhammad Azam Khan issued the judgment. The bench had announced its short order on September 14 after hearing Attorney General for Pakistan Mansoor Awan, Additional Attorney General Amir Rehman, the advocate generals of the four provinces and Islamabad, and counsel for the petitioner, Barrister Akhter Cheena. The court described the case as requiring an “unusual degree of constitutional balance” between the right of political parties and citizens to assemble peacefully and express dissent, and the rights of other citizens to life, liberty, dignity, free movement, trade, business, property, and access to hospitals, educational institutions, courts and workplaces. “The question is not whether a political party is entitled to protest. It plainly is, subject always to the Constitution and law,” the judgment observed. The court held that the right to peaceful assembly could not be exercised in a manner that infringed the fundamental rights of other citizens. A key objection raised by the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa advocate general concerned the territorial jurisdiction of the IHC over provincial authorities functioning outside Islamabad. Rejecting the objection, the court held that Article 199(1)(c) empowered a high court to issue directions where a governmental power or function was being exercised “in, or in relation to” territory within its jurisdiction. The court clarified, however, that the provision did not confer general supervisory jurisdiction over another province. A high court could issue directions to an authority outside its territorial seat where the governmental function had a direct and proximate legal relation with territory within its jurisdiction and intervention was necessary to protect fundamental rights there. The bench also observed that where executive action or inaction was likely to infringe the fundamental rights of citizens within Islamabad, the court was under a “bounden duty” to assume jurisdiction under Article 199(1)(c). The court also rejected the objection that the petition was not maintainable because KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi had not been impleaded as a respondent. It noted that the Advocate General KP was representing both the provincial government and the chief minister. The court further rejected the argument that the petitioner had an adequate alternate remedy under the Peaceful Assembly and Public Order Act, 2024. It noted that no application had, admittedly, been filed under Section 3 of the Act and observed that its provisions had not been adhered to by the KP chief minister and others who had announced their intention to march towards Islamabad. The judgment extensively referred to the Supreme Court’s decision in the Faizabad sit-in case, observing that the constitutional right to assemble and protest was protected but remained subject to restrictions where its exercise infringed the fundamental rights of others. The IHC also referred to the Supreme Court judgment concerning the PTI march of May 25, 2022, noting that assurances regarding a peaceful rally and non-obstruction of the Srinagar Highway had not been honoured. The judgment referred to damage to public and private property, fires in the Blue Area greenbelt, injuries to police personnel and the subsequent invocation of Article 245 to call in the armed forces in aid of civil power. The court also cited its November 21, 2024 order directing that no protest, rally or sit-in be allowed in violation of the Peaceful Assembly and Public Order Act. It observed that the order had also been flouted. During the proceedings, the court allowed the Islamabad deputy commissioner/district magistrate to place electronic material on record. Video clips of the 2022 and 2024 protests were played before the bench, which described the conduct shown in the footage as “highly disturbing and reflective of violence and aggression”. The court noted that PTI was in power in KP during both episodes and observed that provincial government resources had been used in pursuit of political objectives. Regarding the proposed September 27 march, the court held that the petitioner’s apprehension was not merely speculative. It noted that the date and destination of the proposed gathering were known and that statements attributed to the KP chief minister indicated that the date was firm and that he intended to lead the march. While disposing of the petition, the court directed that no political party, political leader, provincial government or public office holder could lawfully occupy roads, highways, interchanges, toll plazas, buildings or similar public places within, or leading to or from, Islamabad in a manner that obstructed free movement or hindered trade, business, professions or access to medical and educational facilities. The provincial governments and chief ministers were directed to ensure that no government resources, public funds, officials, vehicles, machinery or equipment were used directly or indirectly to facilitate any march, rally or procession towards Islamabad. They were also directed to ensure that no public servant was compelled, coerced or induced to participate in such activities. The chief secretaries, police chiefs, federal interior secretary, chief commissioner and IG Islamabad were ordered to issue instructions prohibiting officials from complying with orders requiring them to facilitate such marches. Officials facing coercion were directed to report the matter to the relevant authorities, while helplines or other communication mechanisms were ordered to be established for this purpose. The court further directed the authorities to take departmental action against officials who violated the directions. In a significant finding, the court held that any person whose activity resulted in a violation of the fundamental rights of citizens in Islamabad would be deemed to have violated the Constitution and would be liable for consequences under the law. It further declared that any public office holder whose activity resulted in a violation of citizens’ fundamental rights would be deemed to have violated both the Constitution and his or her oath of office.

Researchers used Claude to breach OpenAI's internal systems. A security research company said Friday it managed to break into OpenAI’s internal systems using the latest software from Anthropic, exposing how quickly the technology can carry out sophisticated cyberattacks. The researchers from security firm Hacktron said they found a security flaw in OpenAI’s public help forum, run by the Discourse platform, that allowed them to take control of the site. “We immediately reported the initial vulnerability to OpenAI and Discourse and worked with them to coordinate the patch,” Hacktron said in a blog post . “We appreciate their attention to detail and fast resolution of this issue,” the post added. OpenAI confirmed the flaw was fixed within about 14 hours of being notified and paid the researchers a $6,500 reward. “We thank the researchers for contacting us and sharing their findings. We narrowed the permissions on Community sign-in tokens and revoked affected tokens and sessions,” said Drew Pusateri, an OpenAI spokesperson. The Hacktron researchers said they initially used Anthropic’s Claude Opus 4.8 to identify and exploit the software flaw, but struggled to make it work consistently. After Anthropic released Claude Opus 5, the researchers said the newer model produced a working hack within about three hours. The hackers did not use Claude Mythos , a more capable Anthropic model that is restricted to a small group of vetted cyber-defence organisations. Anthropic has described Mythos as having the strongest cybersecurity capabilities of any model it has built. Hacktron said the underlying software flaw is not unique to OpenAI and is used across many companies’ products, including those made by Slack and Meta. The firm said it is continuing similar tests at other companies. The case adds to growing concern among security experts that AI tools are making it faster and cheaper to carry out sophisticated cyberattacks that once required specialised teams and months of work.

Lawyers’ body to boycott Islamabad court proceedings on Saturday in protest against Imaan, Hadi’s rearrest. ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad Bar Association (IBA) has announced a boycott of court proceedings in the federal capital on Saturday (September 19) to protest the rearrest of human rights lawyer Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha, after the Supreme Court suspended their sentences and ordered their release on bail. Imaan and Hadi were arrested late on Thursday in a second case after the SC ordered their release in a case pertaining to their posts on social media. The couple was sentenced to 17 years on multiple charges under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca) in the case. However, soon after their release on Thursday, Islamabad police personnel arrested the two outside Adiala jail in connection with another case and produced them before an anti-terrorism court, which sent them to jail on judicial remand. The second case was registered at the federal capital’s Kohsar police station on March 22, 2025 on a complaint by City Magistrate Ghulam Murtaza Chandio. Imaan and her husband were accused of chanting anti-government slogans and blocking roads and were named in the first information report (FIR). The IBA expressed concern over the couple’s rearrest in a statement on Friday and announced that lawyers would not appear before any court in the capital on Sept 19 (Saturday). The bar association said the arrest undermined the sanctity of judicial proceedings and amounted to a violation of fundamental rights and the rule of law. It also expressed strong reservations over the practice of arresting individuals in connection with “unknown” FIRs. The IBA held that any attempt to circumvent or frustrate court orders was unacceptable. It demanded the immediate release of Imaan and Hadi and called for complete details of the cases and circumstances surrounding their arrests to be made public. The association vowed to take every possible measure to safeguard judicial independence, uphold the rule of law and protect fundamental human rights. Amnesty International, HRCP demand immediate and unconditional release Global rights watchdog Amnesty Inter­national condemned the arrest and held that the action demonstrated “authorities’ willingness to weaponise the legal system against critical voices”. “Imaan and Hadi’s re-arrest dispels any pretence that the charges against them are anything other than a politically motivated attempt to punish them for their human rights work,” rights body’s South Asia director, Babu Ram Pant, said in a statement. Pant held that charges were “not only absurd, but an insult to their lifelong commitment to human rights”. The official called on the Pakistani authorities to release the couple immediately and “unconditionally, with no further charges to prolong their detention”. “Imaan and Hadi should be free to meet their friends and family and to do the work they love – representing victims of human rights violations.” Meanwhile, the Human Rights Commission of Pakistan, in a post on X, also demanded Imaan and Hadi’s release and withdrawal of all cases against them.

Govt to stop anyone marching on Islamabad 'in every possible way', says Naqvi. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said on Friday that the government would stop anyone from marching towards the federal capital “in every possible way” and file contempt of court proceedings against those who violated a recent Islamabad High Court (IHC) decision . He was addressing a press conference in Islamabad alongside other officials. The interior minister’s remarks came in the wake of PTI’s call for a nationwide protest , including in Islamabad, on September 27 to demand the release of party founder Imran Khan and mobilise people for the supremacy of the Constitution. Last week, the administrations of the twin cities of Rawalpindi and Islamabad started preparations to counter the PTI’s announced countrywide protest, including a request for detention of activists, arranging containers, seeking additional personnel and procuring anti-riot gear. At the outset of his press conference on Friday, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said a detailed meeting had been held to discuss the upcoming protest call and the law and order situation. Officials from all provinces and federal law enforcement agencies had also attended the meeting. “In light of the detailed IHC judgment, there is no possibility of ravaging the federal capital or any other province,” he said. The minister said that if anyone took to the streets, the government would first pursue legal action by filing a contempt petition against them for violating the IHC order. At the same time, he said, “We will stop the marchers in every possible way.” All law enforcement agencies had been informed of the decision “with all clarity”, Naqvi added. He said weapons had been used and losses suffered in protests in the past. “This time, we are communicating very clear rules of engagement to our law enforcement agencies. They will not remain silent if a bullet is fired at them,” he said. He urged the protesting party’s leadership to hold demonstrations in their respective provinces and cities. “Plans for locking down the capital or charging into another province will never be allowed,” he said. “It is our responsibility to stop this protest to ensure the protection of the lives and property of the capital’s residents,” the interior minister said. The interior minister drew a distinction between a political protest aimed at pursuing political interests and a violent campaign involving people armed with weapons. “There is complete clarity. The organisers of this march will be held accountable if even a single life is lost,” he said. Naqvi said there were still some “sensible” voices within the opposition and hoped they would reconsider their decision. “There is only loss in it, no sort of gain at all,” he added. He reiterated that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had repeatedly invited the opposition from the floor of parliament to hold talks on all issues. “If you want to resolve matters through violent mobs, we are ready for it,” he said. The interior minister reaffirmed that the government had finalised its preparations and all law enforcement agencies were ready. “We will not allow people to spread turbulence as happened in the past,” he said. In a detailed judgment issued today, the IHC ruled that any activity resulting in infringement of citizens’ fundamental rights amounts to a violation of the Constitution. It warned that public office holders responsible for such violations would also be deemed to have breached their oath of office. The court also held that the right to peaceful assembly could not be exercised in a manner that infringed the fundamental rights of other citizens. Kohat attack Commenting on the attack in Kohat, Naqvi said security agencies had been fighting terrorism in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. “We have to focus on this, rather than making strategies for mobilising masses, arranging transport and collecting money,” he said. “After such incidents, it doesn’t suit you to call for long marches and, on the other hand, lift the dead bodies of martyrs,” he added. He further said the KP chief minister and his cabinet should work towards eradicating terrorism with the same spirit with which they were carrying out campaigns for long marches. Earlier today, at least 21 people, including 15 police officials, were martyred when an explosives-laden vehicle detonated near a mosque in Kohat Police Lines . More than 80 people were injured, according to the officials. The incident was followed by terrorists storming the compound and attacking police facilities, according to senior police and district health officials.

Karachi police claim to unearth international meth supply network, arrest two. KARACHI: Police on Friday claimed to have unearthed an international narcotics network involved in the supply of ice — methamphetamine, also known as crystal meth — with the arrest of two of its members, including a woman. Speaking at a press conference in Karachi, East Deputy Inspector General of Police (DIG) Dr Farrukh Ali said Landhi police, acting on a tip-off, had arrested two suspected members of the network. The police also recovered 19.56 kilograms of meth from their possession, he added. The DIG said the suspects were in contact with a notorious Afghan drug dealer, Sabir Afghan. “The held suspects belonged to an Afghanistan-linked network of drug dealers who supplied narcotics in Karachi and other parts of the country,” DIG Dr Ali claimed. He alleged that it was an organised network that supplied drugs from Afghanistan through different routes to Lahore and other parts of Punjab, from where they were subsequently distributed to other parts of the country, including Karachi. DIG Dr Ali said the “international network” was essentially a family-based cartel whose linchpin was a woman named Mehwish, who lived in Lahore. “Mehwish used to supply high-quality ice from Afghanistan, which was then distributed throughout the country,” he said, adding that the arrested woman, was Mehwish’s sister-in-law. The woman’s husband supplied the ice, while the wife distributed it to customers, the senior official claimed. “This family consists of working- or middle-class people. One member of the cartelwas recently arrested by the Anti-Narcotics Force (ANF),” he said. He said further investigation was under way to obtain information from the suspects about their drug network and accomplices. In a lighter vein, DIG Dr Ali said the family-based cartel could be dubbed “Pinky Two”, as it had also maintained the same level of secrecy as Anmol, alias Pinky, who is currently facing trial in Karachi. Anmol was arrested in May in connection with two cases registered at the Garden police station pertaining to the possession of drugs and an unlicensed weapon. She had already been booked in multiple other criminal cases prior to her arrest. The incident gained attention when a video of her being escorted to court without handcuffs went viral on social media. Since her arrest, Anmol has been presented in court amid heavy police presence. During her court appearances, she has also alleged that she has been facing pressure from the police “to take names ” of politicians and other influential persons. Earlier in the month, police also claimed to have recovered a huge quantity of ice and arrested eight suspects in an intelligence-based raid on a warehouse in Mehran Town in Korangi.

Supreme Court admonishes Sindh police over delays in filing FIRs. ISLAMABAD: The Supreme Court on Friday expressed strong displeasure over delays in the registration of first information reports (FIRs) in Sindh, cautioning police officials that they could face contempt proceedings over any future delays. A two-judge SC bench, comprising Justice Muhammad Hashim Khan Kakar and Justice Salahuddin Panhwar, upheld the life sentence of a man convicted of a 2012 murder in Sindh’s Dadu district while hearing the jail petition of Ali Raza Siyal, who had challenged the Sindh High Court’s Aug 24, 2023, Circuit Bench at Larkana judgment upholding his sentence. “We observe with dismay, once again, the consistent practice of delayed registration of FIRs in the province of Sindh,” Justice Salahuddin Panhwar observed in a seven-page judgment, adding that despite earlier directions — and even after the Sindh inspector general had appeared before the court — the practice showed no sign of abating. In this case, the FIR was registered after a delay of more than three days. Although information had been furnished the same night, the judgment expressed regret and recalled that it had called these delays out in the 2026 Muhammad Bux case . The court had directed all inspectors general of police in Pakistan to ensure the prompt registration of an FIR once the officer in charge of a police station was informed about an incident, noting that the officer was duty-bound to register the FIR without delay. The SC also cited the Muhammad Bux judgment, which held that the criminal justice system had evolved and that time was of the essence in the investigation of criminal matters. It further observed that delays could result in the loss or deterioration of forensic evidence, ultimately prejudicing the merits of a case. Consequently, Justice Panhwar ordered the Sindh prosecutor general to furnish a report on all murder cases from Jan 1, 2025, to date, setting out the time of occurrence against the time of reporting and identifying cases in which the FIR was registered after 24 hours. “The report will be submitted within two months for perusal in our chambers,” the judgment directed. At the same time, the judgment directed the SC registrar to ensure that the Muhammad Bux judgment was translated into Sindhi for the understanding of the general public in Sindh and uploaded to the court’s website. “Let it be assured that any further defiance of the judgment of the Supreme Court in Muhammad Bux, from this date onwards, may invite contempt proceedings against the inspectors general of police, the superintendents of police (investigation) and the concerned sub-divisional police officers,” the judgment cautioned. Additionally, the judgment also recalled that the FIR in the present case carried the expression “ faryaadi ”, which the apex court in the Muhammad Bux judgment had also expressly discouraged since it depicted a colonial mindset. In the Muhammad Bux case, the apex court observed that the term “ faryaadi ”, used in police proceedings in Sindh, originated from the Persian word “ faryad ”, meaning cry, help or lamentation, as noted in the Persian dictionary. “Needless to say that the citizen approaches the authorities as a matter of right and not as a matter of mercy,” the judgment emphasised. Similarly, the phrase ‘ bakhidmat janaab SHO’ was a common salutation used in applications addressed to the station house officer (SHO) and also lacked legal backing and implied a subordinate tone. “We concur that it’s actually the SHO, who serves the citizens, not the other way around,” the Supreme Court ruled. Justice Panhwar noted that, in the case at hand, the record itself demonstrated that the police had knowledge of a cognisable offence on the same night but did not register an FIR until more than three days later. “When the record discloses that the officer in charge, knowing of a cognisable offence, delayed registration of an FIR, the trial court is competent and, in a proper case, obliged to take notice of that conduct and proceed in accordance with law, including under Section 201 of the PPC if the ingredients are made out, and to refer the matter to the inspector general of police for departmental action,” the judgment added. It further said that every trial court would be aware of any deliberate delay in the filing of an FIR. Where such a delay was attributable to the police and apparent from the record, it would not be treated as a “mere irregularity”, the SC ruled, adding that the trial court would record a finding on the cause of the delay and take such action as the law permits. In conclusion, the apex court dismissed the jail petition, finding no ground for granting leave. Last September, the SC ruled that no reason could justify the dereliction of the mandatory statutory duty of the police, as violations would erode public trust in the criminal justice system. A three-judge bench of the apex court, comprising Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar, Justice Athar Minallah and Justice Panhwar, also noted that the registration of an FIR under Section 154 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) was exclusively an executive function and that violation of the statutory duty has profound consequences for the parties involved in a criminal case. “A dysfunctional criminal justice system for citizens who are not privileged or powerful manifests [a] lack of constitutional governance. The onus is on the respective governments to establish that every citizen is dealt with in accordance with the obligation enshrined under Article 4 of the Constitution ,” it added.

Govt reaches out to JI, invites party to another round of talks to break deadlock. LAHORE: Federal Minister for Planning Ahsan Iqbal on Friday contacted Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) Vice Emir Liaqat Baloch and invited the party to another round of talks over its demand for the abolition of the petroleum levy. The government’s renewed contact came as JI Emir Hafiz Naeemur Rehman finalised preparations for the party’s Sept 20 march on Islamabad against the levy. According to the JI, Iqbal invited the JI committee, led by Baloch, to talks on Saturday. Baloch said he would respond to the invitation after consulting the party chief and senior leadership. He, however, made it clear that the JI’s protest movement would continue until the petroleum levy was abolished. The latest contact came after several rounds of talks between the government and the JI. The government delegation had initially travelled to Mansoora in Lahore to invite the JI for negotiations, while four subsequent rounds were held in Islamabad. The last round took place on Wednesday, Sept 16. JI claims its proposals can save trillions JI chief Rehman on Friday said the party’s protest movement aimed to press the government for immediate economic relief, asserting that the national exchequer could save between Rs3 trillion and Rs4 trillion if the authorities adopted the party’s proposed fiscal reforms. Addressing a press conference in Islamabad, the JI chief voiced sharp criticism of rising fuel costs and heavy taxation, as well as what he characterised as superficial relief packages that failed to address the core burdens facing the public. Rehman announced that a nationwide “super long march” towards the federal capital would commence on September 20. He rejected the government’s argument that recent energy and fuel price hikes were strictly attributable to international market forces, saying the authorities were relying on aggressive levies to meet revenue targets rather than reducing state expenditure. The JI chief noted that local fuel prices had risen significantly faster than those in neighbouring countries during recent regional tensions, disproportionately affecting lower- and middle-income households that rely heavily on smaller vehicles. Calling for an end to guaranteed profit margins for oil marketing companies at the expense of consumers, Rehman reiterated the JI’s demands to abolish the petroleum levy, end non-productive capacity payments to independent power producers (IPPs) and regasification plants, and fix the price of petrol at Rs225 per litre. Outlining key economic measures, the JI emir called for an immediate cut of three percentage points in the benchmark interest rate, pointing out that every one-percentage-point reduction would save the exchequer approximately Rs574 billion. He said the government must stop protecting commercial bank profits and instead work towards systematically eliminating interest from the national economy. “The public’s support for the party’s movement is growing,” Rehman said, confirming ongoing dialogue and mutual political support with farmers’ alliances and PTI over their respective demonstrations. “The September 20 demonstration will involve caravans travelling to Islamabad from across Sindh, Punjab, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, including a dedicated contingent travelling by train from Karachi,” he said. Rehman assured the public that the self-funded march would not involve road blockades or cause unnecessary disruption to daily life, adding that its arrangements would not obstruct students appearing for the upcoming Medical and Dental College Admission Test (MDCAT). While expressing readiness for immediate talks if the government presented actionable proposals, the JI leadership warned that stalling tactics would not be tolerated as public mobilisation intensified.

15 cops among 21 martyred in blast at Kohat Police Lines, more than 80 injured. PESHAWAR: At least 21 people, including 15 police officials, were martyred on Friday when an explosives-laden vehicle detonated near a mosque in Kohat Police Lines, followed by terrorists storming the compound and attacking police facilities, according to senior police and district health officials. District Health Officer Dr Nasir Hassan Afridi confirmed the toll to Dawn , adding that more than 100 people were injured, with three in critical condition. According to officials, SP Traffic Akbar Shinwari and Dr Israel Orakzai, head of the children’s department at DHQ KDA Kohat, were among those martyred in the attack. Police said at least one attacker was holed up inside the compound and a clearance operation was underway. In a separate statement, the CTD said the Additional IG CTD reached the site of the Kohat attack. An exchange of fire between CTD personnel and the terrorist was ongoing, the department said, adding that the AIG had entered the police lines to take part in the operation and lead the personnel. Later in the evening, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Inspector General (IG) Zulfiqar Hameed visited the police lines as the clearance operation continued. According to a statement, the IGP met GOC Kohat, the regional police officer, the district police officer Kohat and other officers and personnel present at the site. The attack According to IG Hameed and police statements, the attack began when a vehicle-borne improvised explosive device (VBIED) detonated at the boundary wall near the mosque inside the Kohat Police Lines. At least seven attackers then breached the compound and headed towards the CTD and Special Branch buildings. Six attackers, including a suicide bomber, were killed by law enforcers, according to a police statement. At least one attacker was subsequently cornered, prompting police personnel to launch a clearance operation. At around 3:30pm, police said the operation was “in its final stages”. “The operation will continue until the complete elimination of Fitna-ul-Khawarij ,” the IG was quoted as saying, adding that the police’s morale remained high. Fitna al Khawarij is a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan. Earlier, television footage from the scene showed citizens gathered beside a building with a collapsed wall, digging through the rubble and helping the injured. The blast caused extensive damage to the mosque. The attack was claimed by the Hafiz Gul Bahadur-led Ittehadul Mujahideen. Separately, KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi sought a detailed report on the incident, saying the targeting of innocent citizens was “deeply regrettable and unacceptable,” as per a statement issued by his office. Residents gather on a street leading to a police facility, where ambulances are parked following a suicide attack in Kohat on September 18. — Reuters He directed authorities to ensure immediate treatment for the injured. “The nation’s morale cannot be dampened by cowardly acts of terrorism,” he was quoted as saying. The funeral prayers for 15 police personnel martyred in the Police Lines blast were offered in Kohat later in the evening, after which their bodies were transported to their native districts of Kohat, Karak, Lakki Marwat, Bannu and Mardan in Rescue 1122 ambulances. In 2010, 20 people, mostly the relatives of policemen, were killed and more than 90 injured in a remote-controlled bomb blast inside a police colony located just behind the Kohat Police Lines. Condemnations pour in President Asif Ali Zardari, condemning the incident, vowed that the complete elimination of foreign-sponsored terrorists was “essential for national security”. President Zardari wished the injured a swift recovery. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif sought a report on the blast from the concerned authorities. He also directed authorities to expedite relief operations, Radio Pakistan reported. KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi also condemned the blast, praying for the recovery of the injured. “The entire nation stands with the security forces to eradicate terrorism,” he said in a statement. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said in his condemnation that terrorists’ “cowardly acts cannot weaken the nation’s resolve”. A statement posted on his ministry’s X account said Naqvi expressed grief over the loss of lives in the attack and extended condolence to the bereaved. “The nation is standing with the families of the martyrs in this moment of grief,” he was quoted as saying. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi also strongly condemned the suicide attack in Kohat and expressed his condolences over the deaths of police personnel and civilians. In a video message, he said the people of KP had sacrificed more than 80,000 lives for Pakistan and continued to bear the brunt of the fight against terrorism. “Khyber Pakhtunkhwa is Pakistan’s frontline province in the war against terrorism,” he said, adding that peace in Islamabad and the rest of the country was due to the sacrifices made by the people of the province. He also criticised those who, he said, labelled the people of KP as terrorists, saying such remarks reopened their wounds and disrespected their martyrs. Referring to comments by the chief minister of another province , Afridi said it was regrettable to suggest that the threat to Pakistan came from its other provinces rather than India. He said KP and the other provinces were patriotic and had made sacrifices for the country. “Pakistan is our country, and we will not allow any conspiracy to succeed,” he said, adding that efforts to create division, prejudice and hatred among the people would be thwarted. United Kingdom’s High Commissioner in Pakistan said she was “appalled by the horrific attack” in Kohat. “Nobody should face violence in a place of worship“,” she said, adding that her thoughts were with those injured and those who lost loved ones in the attack. China’s embassy in Pakistan said it was “deeply saddened” by the terrorist attack. It condemned the attack and added that it extends “deepest condolences to the deceased victims and sincere sympathies to the breaved families”. Russia’s embassy in Pakistan also strongly condemned the attack. “This terrible tragedy, which claimed numerous lives, once again underscores the need for concerted efforts to combat terrorism in all its forms and manifestations. We hope that those responsible for this heinous act will be identified and brought to justice.” The mission added that their hearts go out to the families and friends of the victims. “We wish a speedy recovery to all those injured.”

Senate panel calls for accountability in allocation of state advertising. ISLAMABAD: The Senate Stan­ding Committee on Information and Broadcasting on Friday called for stricter accountability in the allocation of state advertising. Chairman of the Committee Senator Sarmad Ali suggested that government advertisements for media organisations not registered with the EOBI should be stopped. The committee decided to seek an in-depth briefing from EOBI on the matter in its upcoming meeting. During discussion on the state of the media sector, Chairman of Committee Senator Sarmad Ali stressed the need for immediate support to strengthen the industry in the larger public interest. He said, “financial support in the shape of advertising should be provided to the mainstream media industry to combat fake news”. The committee members noted the National Press Trust purpose ceased to exist after the privatisation of its newspapers. Chairman of the committee while questioning the continuation of the Trust in its present form, remarked that the purpose of the Trust needs to be revisited. He directed that details regarding the National Press Trust’s property and funds should be presented in the next meeting. Suggestion made to stop govt advertisements for media organisations not registered with EOBI The committee decided to seek views of the law ministry on amending the NPT deed in line with changed ground realities and for the welfare of the media workers. It also decided to visit Karachi to ins­pect buildings of the NPT, PTV and Radio Pakistan to review plans for their effective utilisation. On the issue of welfare of media workers, the committee was informed that health insurance for journalists and media workers has been revived, while provision of life insurance is also being considered. The committee considered the Pakistan Broadcasting Corporation (Amendment) Bill, 2025, introduced by Senator Muhammad Abdul Qadir in the Senate sitting held on Dec 1, 2025. The proposed legislation seeks to amend the composition of the Pakistan Broadcasting Corporation Board by providing representation to parliamentarians, including one member from the Senate to be nominated by the Chairman of Senate and one member from the National Assembly to be nominated by the Speaker of the National Assembly. After detailed discussion, the Committee voted on the bill and apart from Senator Pervaiz Rashid all other members present voted in favour of the Pakistan Broadcasting Corporation (Amendment) Bill, 2025, and accordingly it was passed by the committee. Published in Dawn, September 19th, 2026

Ready for the future?. A RECENT McKinsey report outlines three forces reshaping organisations globally — technology and artificial intelligence (AI), economic and geopolitical disruption, and a changing workforce. These forces may appear less immediate to Pakistani business leaders, who already contend with volatile costs, uncertain demand, disrupted supply chains and regulatory uncertainty, amongst other existential issues. With these new challenges, naturally, the question arises: how prepared are our organisations for change? It is a crucial question, but I believe a more fundamental one lies beneath; are Pakistani organisations ready to learn? This shift in focus stems from my belief that organisations should prioritise building capability over simply adopting the latest technology or management ideas. Capability encompasses an organisation’s accumulated ability to achieve its purpose; making sound decisions, developing people, learning from experience and adapting to changing circumstances. Results are undoubtedly important — profit, growth, market share, impact and productivity — but they alone do not define good management. The more important question is whether an organisation is becoming more capable of fulfilling its purpose. Are they making better decisions? Are their people developing? Does experience influence behaviour? Can they respond to environmental changes? And would they continue to perform even if their most senior leader were no longer present? With new challenges, a fundamental question arises: are Pakistani organisations prepared to learn? These questions hold particular relevance for Pakistan. We boast many highly capable founders, family-business leaders and senior executives whose market knowledge, relationships and judge­­­ment have often propelled successful enterprises throu­­gh challenging times. However, personal capability alone does not equate to institutional capability. I have witnessed organisations where every significant decision ultimately falls to the owner(s) or the most experienced person. This applies to difficult customers, major investments, hiring decisions and operational problems — everyone waits for the person who is assumed to know the answer. While this can work well in the short term, with a capable individual at the centre, it leads to a growing dependence on that single person. Managers become adept at escalating problems rather than solving them, and experience becomes concentrated in a few heads rather than embedded in systems, processes and shared judgement. The organisation might grow larger or become more profitable, but it has not necessarily become stronger. True leadership is not measured by whether everything functions when the leader is present; it is whether the organisation has become more capable in their absence. This is one reason Pakistani organisations often struggle with succession. We tend to think of succession as simply finding the next CEO or family member, but it is a much broader question. Has the organisation developed people capable of making decisions? Has it created systems that do not rely on personal intervention? Has it made knowledge accessible beyond those who acquired it? Has it given capable younger managers real exposure to challenging work before they are expected to lead? If not, the organisation may have found a successor, but it has not built succession. The same issue arises with AI. Many leaders are asking which tasks AI can automate, which is a reasonable starting point. However, the more important question is what new capabilities the organisation will need when routine work changes. Technology matters. AI will change how work is done, which skills matter and what customers expect. But technology does not transform an organisation. People using technology differently might. A company can buy the latest systems, appoint a chief digital officer and run pilots in AI. It can still make the same slow decisions, hide the same bad news, reward the same behaviour and depend on the same few senior people. In that case, technology may simply make the organisation more efficient at doing what is becoming less relevant. These are management issues, not technology ones. They also explain why so many transformation programmes disappoint. An organisation announces a new strategy, redraws reporting lines, creates a digital team, brings in consultants and launches a new performance management system. Each of these might be sensible but none automatically changes how the organisation behaves. If people were afraid to speak honestly before the transformation they will remain afraid afterwards. If bad news is softened before reaching senior leadership a new dashboard will simply pre­­sent a cleaner version of the same reality. If managers are rewarded only for their personal results they will have little incentive to develop others. An organisation learns only when experience changes its behaviour. This requires leaders to protect the flow of difficult information. No institution can learn from a reality it is afraid to see. Leaders must distinguish respect for experience from obedience to hierarchy. Older leaders bring perspective while younger people often understand emerging technologies, customers and expectations more instinctively. Healthy organisations create a conversation between the two. The old answer to every new question is the clearest sign of institutional ageing. Pakistan’s organisations do not need to imitate every global management trend or become technology companies. They need to become learning institutions — organisations that can use technology without being defined by it, develop people without abandoning accountability, preserve purpose without protecting every old habit and change before failure makes change unavoidable. The question is not whether Pakistani organisations are ready for change and disruption. It is whether they are ready to learn. The writer advises boards and CEOs on strategy, leadership and organisational transformation. Published in Dawn, September 19th, 2026

Houthis urged to halt ‘provocative acts’ in Red Sea. WASHINGTON: Pakistan condemned Houthi attacks on merchant shipping in the Bab al Mandab Strait and called for their immediate cessation, as the UN Security Council held its second discussion on Friday on the escalating threat to the strategic waterway in the wake of renewed hostilities. “We call upon Houthi militia for immediate cessation of these provocative acts which could have dire consequences for maritime security, and regional peace and stability,” Pakistan’s Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Asim Iftikhar Ahmad, told a Security Council meeting convened by Bahrain. The meeting came two days after the Security Council was briefed on the rapidly deteriorating situation around Bab al Mandab, where the Houthis have advanced along Yemen’s western coast and reportedly captured several islands in the southern Red Sea. United Nations Assistant Secretary General Khaled Khiari told the council that the situation in and around the strait had become “increasingly volatile”. Pakistan’s permanent representative to UN reaffirms ‘unwavering support’ for Saudi Arabia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity The UN official called for restoration of navigational rights and freedom in and around the Red Sea and Bab al Mandab in accordance with international law. Ambassador Asim said the Houthi attacks seriously undermined maritime security and threatened peace and development in regional countries, “especially the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia”, which he said was facing “blatant and unprovoked aggression” by the Houthis. He reaffirmed Pakistan’s “unw­a­vering support” for Saudi Arabia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity, security and prosperity, saying that Pakistan stood in “complete solidarity” with its leadership, government and people. The Bahrain-arranged meeting, held under the theme “Safe Seas, Shared Security: Protecting Freedom of Navigation in an Evolving Security Environment”, was chaired by Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani, the country’s foreign minister. In earlier remarks, Bahrain’s representative Jamal Fares Alrowaei condemned “the Houthi escalation that violates the truce” and threatens regional and international security. He said the escalation had also worsened Yemen’s humanitarian crisis by forcing civilians to flee their homes. “It is high time for the Security Council to take a more decisive stance,” he stressed. Saudi representative Saudi Arabia’s representative Abdulaziz M. Alwasil warned that the Houthi escalation threatened Yemen, regional security, international trade and global supply chains. He cited attacks on Abha, Khamis Mushait, Jazan and Najran that injured civilians, as well as renewed attacks on Sept 14 and continued targeting of commercial vessels in the Red Sea. He said the Houthis and militias supporting them were pursuing a policy of “choking the straits”, holding the international community and global economy hostage. Alwasil said protecting vital waterways was a collective responsibility requiring a firm Security Council response. “Saudi Arabia remains committed to de-escalation and peace while reserving its right to defend its territory and citizens,” Alwasil added. China’s representative Sun Lei expressed concern over the rapid escalation and reaffirmed respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Yemen and Saudi Arabia. Opposing attacks on energy and civilian infrastructure, he said protecting shipping in the Red Sea was a common international responsibility and the rights of merchant vessels must be respected. “Securing freedom of navigation requires ending armed conflict and achieving lasting peace,” Sun said, urging all parties to exercise restraint and return to negotiations. Hormuz concerns Ambassador Asim said disruptions to commercial shipping in both Bab al Mandab and the Strait of Hormuz demonstrated that crises at sea could have consequences far beyond the affected regions. “Disruption of commercial shipping and attacks on merchant vessels, both in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al Mandab, has underscored that crises at sea have grave implications for continents and countries,” he observed. “The volatility at these maritime choke points has not only imperilled peace and stability but also skyrocketed energy prices and heightened fears of global food insecurity,” he added. He said the Strait of Hormuz was a critical maritime trade route for the transit of one-third of globally traded crude oil and a significant share of the fertiliser trade. “Pakistan is deeply concerned at disruptions in the Strait, including attacks on commercial shipping,” he said, calling for “an immediate de-escalation of tensions, security of ships and crew members, and restoration of normal passage through the Strait”. Bahrain’s concept note warned that attacks and threats against merchant vessels, the laying of sea mines and interference with navigational rights could rapidly disrupt global energy flows, international trade, food supply chains and humanitarian operations. Pakistan stresses diplomacy Ambassador Asim linked Pakistan’s position on maritime security to its diplomatic efforts following the outbreak of hostilities between Iran and the United States. “Guided by these foundational principles, Pakistan acted as a mediator between Iran and the United States, following the outbreak of hostilities between the two countries,” he said. “With the support of our friends and partners, we spearheaded diplomatic efforts for de-escalation and broader regional stability, culminating in a ceasefire and the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding.” He said Pakistan would continue efforts “for a negotiated settlement of all outstanding issues for an early return to normalcy at sea and land”. “In pursuit of this objective, Pakistan looks forward to working with all peace-loving nations, in region and beyond, for furtherance of maritime peace and security, and safety of commercial shipping and merchant vessels,” he added. Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs389.14 per litre while HSD will cost Rs424.04 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable from Sept 19 (Saturday) to Sept 21 (Monday). According to Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA), the increase is primarily linked to higher petrol and diesel prices in the international market. The regulator said the prices were revised based on international market rates, premiums and other relevant factors. The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. The government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices, including requiring markets to close by 9pm and cutting fuel allocations for official vehicles by 50 per cent for three months. On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices. A statement from the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said owners of two- and three-wheelers would receive relief of Rs100 per litre on a monthly quota of 20 litres, while owners of vehicles up to 800cc would receive the same relief on a monthly quota of 30 litres. On July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

PM widens fuel subsidy, eases weekly limits. • Token validity increased, people can now use Rs500 discount per week • Minister says scheme benefits 24m • Sindh likely to introduce revised market timings ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday approved a revised structure for the public under the fuel relief scheme currently in vogue across the country, expanding it to include more two- and three-wheelers, and easing weekly limits to offer motorists more flexibility in how they use the support. The prime minister, who is currently abroad on an official visit, directed that motorcycles, rickshaws and Qingqi rickshaws up to 20 years old should also be included in the scheme. “All motorcycles, rickshaws and Qingqi rickshaws registered on or after January 1, 2006, will be eligible for registration under the fuel relief scheme,” a press release issued by the Prime Minister’s Office said. In addition, two- and three-wheelers can now benefit from a concession of Rs500 in one week without quantity limits. According to details, where each token previously entitled the holder to five litres of fuel, now people will be able to obtain a token that entitles them to a Rs500 discount. Each token remains valid for a period of seven days from issuance. Eligible citizens will now be able to avail a maximum concession of Rs2,000 per month, through multiple token redemptions According to Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry, around 24 million people are currently benefitting from the fuel relief scheme. Addressing a press conference, the minister detailed steps being taken to ensure that the subsidy scheme is implemented smoothly, saying that parliamentarians and political teams were assisting citizens through facilitation camps that had been formed across the four provinces, as well as Gilgit-Baltistan, AJK and Islamabad. Mr Chaudhry said he had personally visited several facilitation camps in the capital, which were being approached by a large number of people, whose feedback and complaints were being conveyed directly to the teams supervising the package. The minister conceded that some initial issues had emerged in the implementation of the scheme, particularly regarding the payment mechanism for petrol pump owners, but these had been resolved after meetings with the All Pakistan Petroleum Dealers Association. Talking about the austerity measures imposed by the Centre, he said they were meant to reduce government expenditure. Except for vehicles engaged in operational field activities and those of the defence services, fuel allocations for government vehicles had been reduced by 50 per cent, he said. Mr Chaudhry also said that restrictions had also been imposed on new purchases of government vehicles and other items, while official dinners and lunches had been curtailed. He added official foreign trips would not be government-sponsored, and where an official trip was necessary, economy-class travel would be used. Meanwhile, the provinces showed little movement on the question of austerity measures on Friday. Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa seem to still be mulling the measures. However, a senior Sindh government official told Dawn that the decision to revise market and restaurant closure timings in line with the federal government notification is likely to be announced next week. “The government does not want early closure [of markets] this weekend to facilitate traders,” he added. Azfar-ul-Ashfaque in Karachi also contributed to this report Published in Dawn, September 19th, 2026

Guidelines issued for officials to prevent cyberattack. ISLAMABAD: Govern­ment employees and public-sector organisations have been warned against using personal email acco­unts, unapproved devices, commercial cloud services and public AI tools for official or sensitive government information. Titled the “ National Cybersecurity Handbook 2026-27 ”, the document, issued by the National Cyber Emergency Resp­onse Team (PKCERT) and the Ministry of IT and Telecommunications, outlines baseline operational standards for digital security across public-sector entities. According to the handbook, cybersecurity is not solely a technical responsibility but a shared one, as every user can affect the confidentiality, integrity and availability of gov­e­rnment information assets. The handbook’s guidance on artificial intelligence highlights a growing area of cybersecurity risk. Govt warns staff against using personal emails, devices, AI tools It says officials should not enter classified government documents, official emails, source code or citizens’ personally identifiable information into public AI platforms. Government employees are advised to use only AI tools authorised by their departments and to remove names and sensitive information from prompts or uploaded files. AI-generated outputs should also be reviewed by humans for accuracy and potential security implications. The document also warns against installing unapproved AI extensions or plugins and sharing administrative credentials, API keys or passwords with AI tools. One of the key instructions is that official email accounts must be used for government correspondence and departmental work. Personal accounts such as Gmail and Yahoo should not be used except where exceptionally authorised by the department, while official emails must not be forwarded to personal inboxes. The handbook further says official email addr­esses should not be used to register on shopping, gaming or social media websites, while mailing lists and directories should not be shared with unauthorised entities. Only authorised government devices are to be used for official work. Where a personal device is operationally necessary, prior departmental authorisation is required, and the device must meet prescribed security standards. Officials have similarly been instructed to use only sanctioned cloud services and approved applications. The handbook places particular emphasis on the early reporting of cyber incidents. These include unauthorised access atte­mpts, ransomware notes, suspicious emails, unusual deletion or modification of files and unexplained system behaviour. Published in Dawn, September 19th, 2026

Dar for tighter Pak-Turkiye alignment. ISLAMABAD: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Friday urged relevant departments of Pakistan and Turkiye to closely coordinate preparations for the Joint Commission and the 8th session of the High-Level Strategic Cooperation Council to advance the bilateral agenda. Mr Dar made the remarks during a meeting with Ambassador of Turkiye to Pakistan Irfan Neziroglu, during which the two sides discussed bilateral relations and exchanged views on the evolving regional situation. The ambassador briefed the deputy prime minister on progress under various bilateral institutional mechanisms aimed at advancing cooperation across a range of areas following recent high-level interactions between Pakistan and Türkiye. The deputy PM reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to further deepening engagement with Turkiye in key priority areas and emphasised the need for continued coordination between the relevant departments of both countries. On the regional situation, Mr Dar underscored that dialogue and diplomacy remained the only viable path to resolving issues and achieving lasting peace, stability and prosperity in the region. Attestation probe The deputy PM also took notice of media reports concerning alleged irregularities in the apostille and document attestation system and constituted a three-member inquiry committee to investigate the verification process at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The committee has been tasked with identifying any misuse or irregularities in the apostille and document attestation system, reviewing the role of courier services involved in the process.
